parsed.draft_response:
Hi there—thanks for flagging this. We can route your DPA clarification request to the appropriate privacy/privacy-legal contact for review.

Before we forward it, could you please confirm the following so we send the right information to the right team?
1) The DPA document/version being reviewed (title/date or a link)
2) The specific items they need confirmed for subprocessors (e.g., any named subprocessors or the exact clause/text)
3) The data retention details under review (which retention periods and what data types—product data vs. logs)
4) What you mean by “support logs” in scope (which log sources/fields may include customer identifiers, and whether there’s a retention period they’re reviewing)
5) Your preferred routing contact/channel (name/email) for the “right privacy contact,” or confirm we should route to our general privacy mailbox
6) Any target deadline for the legal review

Once we have the above, we’ll escalate/forward your questions to the privacy team for timely response. 

In the meantime, if you can share the relevant DPA excerpt(s) (especially the subprocessor and retention sections, and the logging language), that will help them respond faster.
promised_actions: Forward the request to the appropriate privacy contact/team after receiving the missing details.
Confirm back to you once the privacy review has been routed/escalated.
safety_notes: Avoid confirming any specific DPA/subprocessor/retention/logging practices until privacy team provides an answer.
Acknowledge human review/escalation without claiming resolution or timelines beyond routing.

grounded_facts: The subject of the ticket is “Need DPA clarification for EU customer data.”
The sender’s legal team is reviewing a DPA before enabling EU customer records.
The legal team needs confirmation on subprocessors.
The legal team needs confirmation on data retention.
The legal team needs confirmation on whether support logs can include customer identifiers.
The ticket requests routing to the right privacy contact.

Which specific “subprocessors” list or contract clause requires confirmation
